title: Akalaka descent tradition
summary: Oral tradition tracing Ikwerre descent from a progenitor named Akalaka.
body: Ikwerre oral tradition names Akalaka as a founding ancestor from whom major clans are said to descend. Multiple community variants exist and should be collected separately rather than merged into a single account.
significance: Anchors Ikwerre clan structure and identity.
place: Rivers State (narrow to community once sourced)

title: Contested origins and the Igboid classification
summary: A second, contested strand of origin/identity accounts tied to the Ikwerre–Igbo question.
body: Some traditions, and the linguistic classification of the Ikwerre language within the Igboid group, are read differently by different communities and scholars. Variant accounts are recorded here as competing entries rather than merged.
significance: Exercises the model's disputed path; central to identity.

title: Settlement of the Niger Delta forest zone
summary: Traditions of Ikwerre settlement in the coastal forest of present-day Rivers State.
body: Oral accounts describe movement into and settlement of the Niger Delta forest zone. Dating is relative (reckoned by generations) and must be treated as approximate.

title: Founding of an Ikwerre community (placeholder: e.g. Elele / Aluu / Igwuruta)
summary: Founding account of a specific Ikwerre community — placeholder pending a sourced community.
body: Individual Ikwerre communities have their own founding accounts and founders. This is a placeholder to be replaced by a specific, sourced community founding; the named community and founder must be verified.
significance: Tests the place link and the founded_by relationship.

title: Eze traditional rulership and councils
summary: The Eze title and community councils in Ikwerre governance.
body: Ikwerre communities are traditionally led by Eze title-holders supported by councils of elders. Specific titles, selection processes, and roles must be verified with traditional authorities.

title: Age-grade system
summary: Age-grades as a unit of social organisation, labour, and defence.
body: Age-grades traditionally organise communal labour, defence, and social duties across Ikwerre communities. Structure and current role to be confirmed with informants.

title: Founding ancestor (name per tradition — to verify)
summary: Placeholder for the founding ancestor named in oral tradition.
body: Oral tradition names a founding ancestor (e.g. Akalaka) from whom clans descend. The specific figure, their relationships, and any succession lines must be collected and verified before use.
significance: Tests the figures table and founded_by / succeeded_by relationships.

title: New-yam festival (Ikwerre name and rites to verify)
summary: A harvest festival marking the new yam — Ikwerre specifics to confirm.
body: A new-yam harvest festival is widely observed across the region. The specific Ikwerre name, timing, and rites must be collected locally rather than assumed from neighbouring peoples.
significance: Tests festival and commemorates / related_to links.

title: Farming, fishing and palm produce
summary: Yam and cassava farming, fishing, and palm produce as mainstays.
body: Ikwerre livelihood traditionally centres on yam and cassava farming, fishing in delta waters, and palm produce. Specifics and change over time to be sourced.

title: Founding of Port Harcourt on Ikwerre/Diobu land
summary: The British founded Port Harcourt (c. 1912–13) on Ikwerre (Diobu) land.
body: Port Harcourt was established by the British colonial administration around 1912–1913 on land of the Ikwerre (Diobu). The exact date and the land history should be confirmed against archival and scholarly sources.
significance: Load-bearing event linking origins, land, and modern identity.

title: The Ikwerre–Igbo identity question
summary: Ongoing, contested question of Ikwerre identity relative to the Igbo.
body: Whether the Ikwerre constitute a subgroup of the Igbo or a distinct people is actively contested and politically charged. All sourced perspectives are to be recorded here as disputed, with no editorial side taken.
significance: Demonstrates disputed handling on a sensitive, load-bearing topic.

title: Palm-nut ('banga') cuisine — Ikwerre specifics to verify
summary: Palm-nut based dishes associated with the region — Ikwerre specifics to confirm.
body: Palm-nut ('banga') based dishes are associated with the Niger Delta. The specific Ikwerre dishes, their names, and preparation should be collected locally rather than generalised from the region.
